5004.d:
Fire Cards is a series of generative artworks inspired by 19th-century Japanese fireworks catalogues. The images in these catalogues didn't so much focus on realism, but on the visual associations of the pyrotechnic effects instead. Using a restricted color palette and relatively simple shapes, this resulted in vibrant, graphical posters that sparked your own imagination more than anything else.

In Fire Cards, the abstract, static images are transformed back into lively, dynamic worlds again, each with their own distinctive, centuries-old aesthetics. Using a custom animation and 2D render system, the algorithmically generated worlds slowly build up and show a magical fireworks performance.

Fire Cards are tiny, personal and unique shows of wonder.

5011.d:
Returns is an offline-first PWA and an interactive SVG. It combines the joy of interaction, digital color and minimalist sculpture with the potential of a long running, continuously unique visual. Based on “Shipping” from 2016, it is inspired by Anne Truitt, Ugo Rondinone, Imi Knoebel, Kelly Ellsworth and many others.

A subdivision slices the viewport influenced by width, height and depth. Corners are cut by replacing them with two new points, pulled towards each other along the edges. Shapes are “rounded" by repeating this step, keeping the new points close together. As colors change, so do the relations between shapes, even if geometry changes at a slower pace. New compositions are created on click or after a timeout. This progress over time allows for infinite iterations within the space of each token. It is the promise of a seeded starting point, plus the potential for unlimited new and unique iterations and states over time.

Restless, tautly-stretched triangles form overlapping circles; sparks of light leaking from the gaps between their attenuated edges. Radial spokes of glimmering starlight play over a subtly-textured background.

Interactivity:

Click the mouse to affect the passage of time; dragging near the edge of the piece brings rapid change; the centre affords more subtlety.

Press 's' in full-screen mode to save an image of the canvas.

Features affecting rarity:

Distortion: Variable levels of distortion, which affects the spikiness of the triangles and light rays. Low and high distortion are more rare.

Offset average: To add variability to potential mints, this reflects the distance between the central dark portion and the lighter portion.

Other features:

Palette: Ten carefully-tuned colour schemes of equal likelihood, with hue, brightness and saturation chosen to showcase the movement and range of the piece whilst maintaining detail.

Background: The two types of background are of equal probability.

Simbol is a digital representation of a tree slice. At each iteration a single tree is generated with specific features that can vary between each output. It is built around 3 elements that mimic real tree features: 

- Tree lines: they represent the age of the tree and may be more or less distorted depending on the tree. Lines can vary in color and opacity. Some lines have a chance to be rendered with dots.

- Knots: They are points of disruption present along some of the lines. They will push and pull the tree line around them and provide more movement to the piece.

- Bark: It’s a frame of thousands of little circle that will coat the outside of a piece and provide a different set of texture and contrast with the smooth lines.

《Griddy》started from a survey of Mondrian’s and Raven Kwok’s work. During the process, several primitive elements are put together to form 《Griddy》.

The palette is chosen from RYB, RGB, CMYK. Three possible thicknesses are chosen for the grid line, and with a possibility of the same color with the background, forming a “negative space” effect. Three ratios for the partition of space, and with a possibility of “inverted ratio” when dividing space. For filling the grid, three prime numbers will be randomly selected for each color. And finally, a possibility that the whole grid moves.

5166.d:
Tension, we all encounter it.

There are 2 styles: basic and complicated. As with life, simplistic connections are rare. However, the criss-crossing and wider web of connections may result in a more beautiful outcome.

Basic style simply loops over the outer ring and assigns a node to a group based on a hash digit (last 10 digits of hash iterated over) to form cliques. Complicated style is built on top of basic style, where more elements are added, resulting in larger cliques and more interesting connections. This number of additional elements is related to the hash value.

Color palette is randomly generated based on hash digits. Hover over a group node to see the connections tied to it.

I have enabled the exploration of variations.

5183.d:
I have always been fascinated by large apartment complexes at night. For this piece, I'm trying to convey the feeling of being just one anonymous person surrounded by thousands of people we don't know. 

The owner of each token gets assigned a random room that will be the only white one among all the others in the sector.

Features are:
- Color: 8 traits
- Moon Size: 3 traits
- Building Density: 3 traits
- Smog Level: 4 traits

Households and Population are calculated based the actual real number of apartment units in the sector.

Room number is accurate and based on room number standards in Japan. It is composed of the floor number and the room number on that floor. Please note that the ground floor is floor 1.

Each building has multiple traits: height, width, floors, rooms by floor, antenna, entrance door.

Each room has multiple traits: rounded, curtains, blinders, lamp, frame, fence, light on or off.

Press ‘enter’ to skip the introduction.
Press ‘s’ to save an image.

5222.d: Musical counterpoint is to me an abstraction of the layered, intertwining rhythms of every activity we carry on in our lives. This series is a metaphorical transposition of the musical counterpoint into a visual space, sometimes with repeating patterns, sometimes with broken structures, sometimes isolated notes / hours / souls.

As wild as it is, for me the sea has something soothing. The rushing of the waves, the strong wind in your face, the salty air, the screeching of seagulls, freezing rain. At the same time, the raging sea can be life-threatening. Many have lost their lives at sea or by the sea, some by flooding, some in the battle for peace, others in search of a better life. 

The sea, with its many faces and stories, is beautiful, terrifying and everything in between.

5232.d:
Uninhabitable is a generative system built only from ellipses. The process of playing with different geometric and trigonometric disruptions gives rise to four different compositions which seek to evoque living constructions and environments. Besides the shape itself and its related distortion, the stroke weight of the lines plays a meaningful role in the piece. Following a discrete range [0.01,0.1,1] the weight reveals the process allowing the viewer to realize the trace of the huge amount of lines in each piece. This back and forth between scales and context is, while kind of stripping the code, part of my continuing interest on understanding the -usually- crazy paths of machines' way of thinking.

Press "h" to see it and high resolution and refresh to get back to the initial state. Press "h" to save it.

Uninhabitable is an original work by Iskra Velitchkova. 2021.
